answer: Time-locked reward vesting resists sybils: rewards an identity earns settle not at once but vest linearly over a long horizon, and any identity flagged fraudulent during the window forfeits all unvested gains. A swarm that farms rewards cannot cash out — each fake's earnings hang like an unripe walnut, and detection before maturity claws them back. The willow-slow schedule forces an attacker to keep every clone alive and unflagged through the whole period to realize value, turning instant mass-minting into a quartz-hard exposure window where audits have time to catch the ring.
